title: Esther Goes Before the King
text:
Esther, a young Jewish woman raised by her cousin Mordecai, had become queen to Ahasuerus, king of Persia, without revealing her people. Then the king's chief minister Haman, enraged that Mordecai would not bow to him, obtained a royal decree to destroy all the Jews of the empire on a single day.

Mordecai sent word to Esther that she must go to the king and plead for her people. She answered that anyone who went to the king in the inner court without being summoned was put to death, unless the king held out his golden scepter, and she had not been called for thirty days. Mordecai replied that she should not think she would escape in the palace. If she kept silent, help would come from somewhere else, but she and her family would perish. "And who knows," he added, "whether you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"

Esther asked all the Jews of Susa to fast for her for three days, as she would. "Then I will go to the king, though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish."

On the third day she stood in the inner court. The king held out the scepter. She invited him and Haman to a banquet, and then to a second. There she revealed who she was and named Haman as the enemy who sought her people's death. The king had Haman hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.
lesson: A position of access or influence is not only a privilege, it is a responsibility. When those who depend on you are in danger, the comfort of your position is not a reason to stay silent.
date: Ancient Jewish tradition, set in the 5th century BC
source: Hebrew Bible, Book of Esther 3 to 7
